faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions about World Cup 2026 Pools
faq.q1: When does the 2026 World Cup start?
faq.a1: The FIFA World Cup 2026 will take place from June 11 to July 19, 2026 in Mexico, the United States and Canada. The opening match will be played at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, and the final will be held at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.
faq.q2: Is it free to create a World Cup pool on Picks4All?
faq.a2: Yes, creating your 2026 World Cup pool on Picks4All is completely free for groups of up to 20 participants. No credit card or payment details required. Just sign up, create your group and invite your friends.
faq.q3: How many teams participate in the 2026 World Cup?
faq.a3: The 2026 World Cup will be the first in history with 48 participating teams, a significant increase from the previous 32-team format. Teams are distributed across 12 groups of 4, and the top two from each group plus the 8 best third-placed teams advance to the next round.
faq.q4: How are points calculated in the pool?
faq.a4: Picks4All lets you configure your pool's scoring system. By default, 3 points are awarded for an exact result, 1 point for a correct winner (or draw), and 0 points for a miss. The organizer can customize these values when creating the group.
faq.q5: Can I invite friends from other countries to my pool?
faq.a5: Absolutely! Picks4All is available in Spanish, English and Portuguese. Your friends from anywhere in the world can join your pool and use the platform in their preferred language. Just share the invitation link.

hero.title: How to create a World Cup 2026 prediction pool
hero.subtitle: The guide you need to set up your World Cup pool on Picks4All

intro.p1: Let's be honest: you've been arguing with your friends for months about who knows more about football. Whether Argentina repeats, whether the host nation makes a deep run, whether that striker is overrated. All talk. The 2026 World Cup is the perfect chance to put your money where your mouth is.
intro.p2: A World Cup prediction pool turns 104 matches into a personal competition between you and your group. Every prediction counts, every goal matters, every upset hurts (or launches you to the top). And the best part: setting one up on Picks4All takes less time than debating a starting lineup.

process.title: Set up your pool in 5 minutes

registration.title: Quick registration
registration.text: Head to picks4all.com and create your account with email or Google. Takes 30 seconds, no endless forms or SMS verifications. Already have an account? Skip ahead.

tournament.title: Select the tournament
tournament.text: Choose World Cup 2026 from the list of available tournaments. The calendar is already loaded with all 104 matches, 16 venues, and official kickoff times. Nothing to configure there.

scoring.title: Choose your scoring system
scoring.text: This is where you give your pool its personality. You have 4 options and each one completely changes the group dynamic. I'll break down the differences further below.

invite.title: Invite your group
invite.text: Picks4All generates an invite code and a direct link. Send it on WhatsApp, drop it in the work Telegram group, or email it out. Everyone who joins can see the matches and start making predictions.

during.title: What happens during the tournament?
during.p1: Before each match, every participant enters their score prediction. Predictions lock automatically before kickoff — the organizer can configure whether it's 10 minutes, 1 hour, or 1 day before. Once locked, nobody can see what others predicted until the match ends.
during.p2: Results come from the official football data API. No human intervention. When the match ends, points are calculated automatically and the leaderboard updates instantly. Nobody can manipulate results — not even the group creator.
during.p3: If the API reports an incorrect result (happens very rarely), the organizer can request a correction. But they have to explain why, and every participant gets a notification about the change. Full transparency.

scoring.title: The 4 scoring systems
scoring.intro: Not all groups are the same. The scoring system determines whether your pool rewards surgical precision or football instinct. Here are the 4 available modes:

basic.name: Basic
basic.description: For purists. You nail the exact score: 3 points. You get the winner right (or draw) but not the scoreline: 1 point. You miss everything: 0. That simple. No complications, no excuses. Perfect for large groups where you want clear rules from match one.

cumulative.name: Cumulative
cumulative.description: Adds an extra bonus when you get the exact goal difference right, even if the scoreline is off. For example, if you predicted 3-1 and it ended 2-0, you didn't get the exact score, but you nailed the 2-goal difference — and that earns you points. Rewards knowledge beyond luck.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Everything from Cumulative, but with phase multipliers. Group stage is worth x1, round of 32 x1.5, quarters x2, semi-finals x2.5, and the final x3. This gives the tournament a dramatic twist: someone trailing can come back with strong knockout predictions. The later rounds feel like do-or-die matches.

custom.name: Custom
custom.description: You decide how many points each type of hit is worth. Want to give 5 points for an exact score and 0 for a correct winner? Go ahead. Want a correct draw prediction to be worth more than a correct win? Also fine. Full control for pools with house rules.

tips.title: Tips from someone who's organized a few
tips.p1: Pick your scoring system before inviting anyone. Seems obvious, but if you already have 15 people in the group and want to change the rules, you'll have a revolt on your hands. Decide first, communicate the rules clearly, then open the doors.
tips.p2: The Advanced system generates the most excitement, but it needs people who'll follow the tournament from start to finish. If your group is casual — half of them will forget to make predictions after the group stage — stick with Basic or Cumulative. The fun is in participation, not complexity.
tips.p3: Send the invite link early. Don't wait until the first match to assemble the group. If people sign up a week ahead, they can explore the platform, understand the rules, and be ready from the opening whistle at the Azteca.
tips.p4: If you have a WhatsApp group, give your pool a name that means something to the group. 'Work pool' is fine, but 'The Coffee Experts' builds more commitment. Competition between friends works better when it has an identity.

hero.title: World Cup 2026 prediction pool rules
hero.subtitle: Everything you need to know about scoring, prediction deadlines, and how the leaderboard works

whatIs.title: What is a prediction pool?
whatIs.p1: It's a prediction game between friends. Before each match, every participant writes down the score they think the match will end with — for example, Argentina 2 - Mexico 1. If they get it right, they earn points. At the end of the tournament, whoever has the most points wins.
whatIs.p2: Depending on where you're from, you might know it by a different name: quiniela in Mexico and Central America, polla in Colombia and Chile, prode in Argentina, penca in Uruguay, porra in Spain, bolao in Brazil. The concept is the same everywhere: prove you know more about football than everyone else.

exact.title: Exact score
exact.text: The jackpot. You predicted 2-1 and it ended 2-1. This is the hardest to get and awards the most points. In the basic system, that's 3 points.

winner.title: Correct winner
winner.text: You didn't nail the scoreline, but you got the winner right (or that it would be a draw). You said Mexico 1-0 and it ended Mexico 3-2: not exact, but you knew Mexico would win. In the basic system, 1 point.

difference.title: Goal difference
difference.text: Only in Cumulative and Advanced modes. If you got the goal difference between the teams right — even if the scoreline was different — you earn a bonus. You predicted 3-1 (difference of 2) and it ended 2-0 (difference of 2): not exact, but your read of the match was on point.

miss.title: Complete miss
miss.text: You said Team A would win and Team B won. You predicted a draw and it was a blowout. 0 points. Happens to everyone all the time — that's part of the fun.

multipliers.title: Phase multipliers
multipliers.intro: In Advanced mode, points are worth more as the tournament progresses. The logic is simple: predicting a group stage result when there are still 48 teams and plenty of information available isn't the same as predicting a semi-final where anything can happen.
multipliers.example: If you nail an exact score in the final (3 base points x3 multiplier), that's 9 points from a single match. A hit like that can flip the entire table. That's why the late rounds in Advanced mode are pure adrenaline.

deadlines.title: Prediction deadlines
deadlines.p1: Each match has a deadline for submitting your prediction. By default, it locks 10 minutes before kickoff. The organizer can change this: 30 minutes, 1 hour, even 1 day before.
deadlines.p2: While predictions are open, you can change yours as many times as you want. Nobody sees what others predicted until the deadline passes. No cheating possible.
deadlines.p3: If you don't submit a prediction before the deadline, you simply don't earn points for that match. No penalty, but no second chances either.

results.title: Where do results come from?
results.p1: Results update automatically from the official football data API. There's no person behind the scenes updating scores by hand. When the referee blows the final whistle, points calculate themselves.
results.p2: The group creator can't invent or freely modify results. If there's an API error (something that very rarely happens), the organizer can request a correction. But they have to write a justification, and every participant receives a notification explaining the change. Everything is on the record.

leaderboard.title: The leaderboard
leaderboard.p1: Points accumulate throughout the entire tournament. After each match, the leaderboard updates automatically. You can see who's leading, how many points each participant has, and how many exact scores they've hit.
leaderboard.p2: In case of a tie between two or more participants, these criteria apply in order: most exact scores, most correct winners, and the order they joined the group (whoever joined first wins the tiebreaker).

cta.text: Now you know the rules. 48 teams, 104 matches, and your football reputation on the line. All that's left is creating your group.

methodology.title: What data powers this prediction
methodology.intro: Our AI processes six data sources to generate these World Cup 2026 predictions. Each factor carries different weight in the model, and the output is a projection that tries to capture what the numbers say about each team. Argentina leads the FIFA ranking with 1867.25 points. France follows with 1859.78. Brazil sits third at 1840.43. But rankings alone don't win World Cups — there are variables you only see when you look beyond the table.
methodology.rankingsDesc: The current top 10: Argentina (1), France (2), Brazil (3), Spain (4), England (5), Portugal (6), Netherlands (7), Belgium (8), Germany (9), Colombia (10). These points reflect official performance over the last 4 years.
methodology.historyDesc: Brazil holds 5 titles. Germany and Italy have 4 each. Argentina has 3, including Qatar 2022. France has 2. Uruguay and England have 1 apiece. Previous championships carry weight because World Cup experience creates a real psychological edge.
methodology.formDesc: Argentina has an 82% win rate in their last 20 official matches. France sits at 71%. Spain at 78% with a possession game that dominates Europe. Brazil has recovered from an irregular stretch and posts a 73% rate.
methodology.squadDesc: How many players from each national team compete in top European leagues and in advanced Champions League stages. High-pressure club experience at the highest level translates to World Cup performance.
methodology.homeDesc: Mexico, the United States, and Canada play at home. Historically, the host nation reaches at least the quarter-finals in 62% of World Cups. Home crowd support, climate familiarity, and no jet lag are measurable factors.
methodology.h2hDesc: Match records between teams over the last two decades. Some nations have clear dominance over specific opponents that isn't reflected in the general ranking.
methodology.aiNote: This prediction was generated by Picks4All's artificial intelligence, combining sports data analysis with prediction models. World Cup 2026 forecasts are updated as final warm-up matches are played.

groups.title: World Cup 2026 group stage prediction
groups.subtitle: Group by group, our AI model projects who advances and who goes home. The top two from each group qualify directly, and the 8 best third-placed teams also reach the round of 32.
groups.analysisA: Mexico has home advantage and the Azteca as a fortress. Czech Republic is a solid side that knows how to pick up points in tough groups. South Korea competes for third with genuine World Cup experience.
groups.analysisB: Switzerland has been one of the most consistent teams of the last cycle, with 4 consecutive knockout stage appearances. Canada plays at home but lacks real World Cup pedigree.
groups.analysisC: Brazil is the clear favourite, but Morocco proved in Qatar 2022 they can compete with anyone. They reached the semi-finals and retain a strong core.
groups.analysisD: The United States plays at home and has invested in development like never before. Turkey has the squad to compete. Paraguay and Australia battle for third.
groups.analysisE: Germany needs redemption after two consecutive group stage exits. With a refreshed squad, the individual talent is there. Ecuador keeps growing as a South American force.
groups.analysisF: Netherlands has one of the deepest squads in the tournament. Japan has cleared the group stage in three consecutive World Cups. Sweden can spring surprises.
groups.analysisG: Belgium remains powerful despite a generational transition. Egypt has Salah as their primary weapon. Iran is hard to beat but struggles to create goals.
groups.analysisH: Spain dominates. The possession, the style, the bench depth. Uruguay is the most dangerous rival — they always perform in World Cups above their ranking.
groups.analysisI: France has, on paper, the most expensive squad in the tournament. Senegal leads African football with a blend of pace and European experience. Norway has Haaland.
groups.analysisJ: Argentina are the defending champions. Austria and Algeria will fight for second — Austria has a better ranking, Algeria more World Cup experience.
groups.analysisK: Portugal with Cristiano likely in his final World Cup. Colombia are FIFA top 10 and have shown a high level in qualifiers. A quality group.
groups.analysisL: England arrives as one of the title favourites. Croatia, runners-up in 2018 and third in 2022, never give up. Ghana needs a heroic effort.

bestThirds.title: The 8 best third-placed teams that advance
bestThirds.subtitle: Of the 12 third-placed teams, 8 qualify for the round of 32. Our AI projects these teams will have enough points and goal difference to advance as best thirds.

knockout.title: Knockout stage — Full prediction
knockout.subtitle: From 32 teams down to 1 champion. The AI model projects each matchup, factoring in performance under pressure, knockout experience, and squad depth for extra time.

champion.label: 2026 World Champion
champion.reasoning: Argentina defends their title with the most complete generation in their history. Messi in his final World Cup, a solid defence with Martinez and Romero, and a midfield that controls matches. The data backs the defending champion: 82% recent win rate, 3 World Cup titles, and the top FIFA ranking.

analysis.title: Detailed analysis: why Argentina wins the 2026 World Cup
analysis.p1: The numbers tell a clear story. Argentina doesn't just lead the FIFA ranking — they've done so continuously since December 2022. That's three and a half years at the top. That's not inertia: it's consistency. Their 82% win rate in the last 20 official matches is the highest of any team in the tournament. France, their closest rival on this metric, sits 11 points behind.
analysis.p2: The Messi factor is undeniable but it's not the only argument. This team has Emiliano Martinez, arguably the best penalty goalkeeper in the world. Romero and Lisandro Martinez as world-class centre-backs. Mac Allister and Enzo Fernandez control midfield with a maturity they didn't have in Qatar. And Alvarez has evolved from substitute to attacking reference.
analysis.p3: Brazil is the most dangerous rival. With Vinicius Jr., Rodrygo, and a new generation playing at the best clubs in Europe, they have the individual talent to beat anyone in a single match. The semi-final between them would be the match of the tournament — two South American styles at their peak, on North American soil.
analysis.p4: France have the squad to reach the final, but they've shown defensive fragility in their recent cycle. Spain dominates possession like no one else, but struggles against teams that sit deep and counter. Germany is a wildcard: they could be brilliant or disappointing. England always goes deep but never quite wins it. In the end, our model says Argentina — but football doesn't read models.
